newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - April 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - April 2.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- TORIES PLAN RADICAL TAX BREAK

Prime minister John Major is to attempt to regain the initiative for the Tories in the general election campaign with the announcement on Wednesday of radical tax proposals. Under the plans, married women who do not work would be allowed to transfer their 3,765 stg tax allowance to their working husbands. The initiative will form the centrepiece of the Conservative party's election manifesto.
-- SURGE IN HOUSING PRICES IS 'NO CAUSE FOR PANIC'

A survey by insurance group Legal and General has found that fears of a new boom and bust cycle caused by surging house prices are misplaced. The study canvassed people's intentions to move, and found no sign of the panic buying and speculation that typified the housing market in the late 1980s. L&G did find that most people expect house prices to rise in the next 12 months, an expectation supported by figures from the Halifax, which said that house prices rose 1 percent in March, taking annual price rises to 7.2 percent.
-- EUROPEAN SHARES FALL AMID FEAR OF END TO BULL RUN

Share prices fell across European markets on Tuesday, prompting claims that Europe's strong bull run may be coming to an end. The decline in prices, which hit France and Germany particularly hard, follows two days of heavy losses on Wall Street. US markets have lost almost 5 percent since European trading closed for the Easter break. Tuesday's movements prompted one analyst, Mark Howdle, head of European equity strategy at UBS, to comment: "The party is over. The correction we have been looking for has begun."
-- OUTSOURCING HELPS TOP IT GROUPS LIFT REVENUES

Figures compiled by Information Technology (IT) industry analyst Richard Holway show that the top ten software and computer services companies increased their UK revenues by 29 percent in 1996, to a total of 4.06 bn stg. The figures were boosted by outsourcing contracts awarded by industry and the public sector, including large deals from Rolls Royce and Airtours for EDS, the US group that is the largest supplier of computer services in the UK.
-- COMPUTER MODEL WILL HELP BANKS RATE CREDIT EXPOSURE

A computer model offering a new method for banks to measure their credit exposure has been developed by US investment bank JP Morgan. The model is to be launched by a group of international banks on Wednesday, offering hope that it could eventually lead to a reduction in the cushion of capital regulators require them to hold. The system allows a bank to quantify the maximum likely loss it could make on its loan portfolio, drawing together different types of risk, such as consumer loans and corporate bonds, into a single number.
-- ORANGE LEADS SUBSCRIBER RACE

Analysts are expecting Orange, the youngest of the UK's four mobile phone operators, to show a net addition of more than 100,000 customers over the past three months when it publishes figures on Wednesday. Such a rate of new connections would be greater than any of Orange's three UK rivals, with market leader Vodafone reporting on Tuesday a net gain in connections of 67,000 for the same three month period. One-2-One and Cellnet, the other operators, are also due to report figures on Wednesday.
-- TRAFFICMASTER PLOTS NEW ROUTE INTO GERMANY

Traffic information provider Trafficmaster is extending its system to Germany following an agreement with German telecommunications group, Mannesmann Autocom. The agreement is to be Trafficmaster's first step into extending its system to continental Europe. Talks with France and the Netherlands are ongoing, with the Trafficmaster system expected to be underway in the two countries in 1998.
-- TELWEST CHIEF GOT PAY-OFF OF 0.54 MILLION STG

Alan Michaels, who left UK cable operator Telewest in August following its successful flotation in London and New York, has been paid 539,000 stg. Michaels' total income was 707,000 stg, and he will receive in addition 434,837 shares under an
executive scheme.
-- TADPOLE SHARES SUSPENDED

UK computer group Tadpole Technology's shares were suspended on Tuesday "pending the publication of the 1995-96 report and accounts". Tadpole, however, claimed the reduction was due to their awaiting the completion of a "significant transaction". Analysts have suggested Tadpole will link up with a larger computer group, swapping equity for cost sharing and a capital injection. The possibility of the company's sale has not been ruled out.
-- SHELL SET TO ANSWER SHAREHOLDERS' ETHICS QUERIES

Shareholders of the Anglo/Dutch oil group Royal Dutch/Shell, who are demanding improvements in the company's environmental practices and business ethics, continue to wait for a response. Shell plans to announce its solutions to the problems next week.
